scope: Authoritative NAIF Deep Space Network station geometry and NASA-reported lunar-flyby timing used to reconstruct topocentric lunar occultation from representative 70-meter reference antennas at each DSN complex.

nasa_public_events.interpretation: Earthset and Earthrise are geometric visual events reported from Orion. Communications LOS and AOS are operational network events. They are related but are not assumed to be identical.

naif_station_reference.station_location_uncertainty_note: NAIF notes that accumulated station-location uncertainty can reach approximately 0.1 m at one sigma for some stations due to tectonic motion and events. This is negligible relative to the kilometer-scale geometry modeled here.

earth_reference.use: Transform propagated station positions from ITRF93 into J2000 and calculate local geodetic elevation.

guardrails: The representative 70-meter antenna at a DSN complex is used as a geometric reference point and is not asserted to be the antenna that operationally tracked Artemis II during the flyby.
Best agreement with NASA public LOS and AOS timing does not identify the actual operational DSN antenna.
Topocentric lunar occultation is necessary geometric context but does not by itself establish RF link availability.
A station below its local geometric horizon is not considered a plausible direct Earth-to-Orion observer at that instant.
NASA public LOS and AOS timestamps are minute-level operational references and are not exact geometric limb-contact measurements.
No antenna gain, link budget, modulation state, network scheduling, handover logic, received signal strength, or tracking assignment is inferred.
Radio-frequency DSN geometry is not used as a prediction of O2O optical communications availability.
